title: Linear Fabrication Annotations
note: Interpretive framing only; not quantitative claims.

annotations.label: MATTER AS RESOURCE
annotations.text: Matter enters the system primarily as something to be extracted, standardised and made available for production.

annotations.label: FORM IMPOSED
annotations.text: Fabrication commonly fixes matter into predetermined forms rather than allowing form to emerge through ongoing material–environment interaction.

annotations.label: DISCOURSE REMOVED
annotations.text: Once fabricated, materials are often expected to remain stable and passive; their capacity to respond, negotiate or adapt is largely excluded from the design process.

annotations.label: FIXED LIFE EXPECTANCY
annotations.text: Products move through prescribed use phases and are often replaced when damaged, obsolete, unfashionable or economically inconvenient to repair.

annotations.label: DEAD-END FLOWS
annotations.text: Many outputs cannot re-enter equivalent material cycles and terminate as landfill, incineration, displaced waste or lower-value recovery.

annotations.label: WEAK CLOSURE
annotations.text: Some loops exist, but they are partial and often depend on downcycling, energy-intensive recovery or infrastructure that is not universally available.

annotations.label: EXTERNALISED CONSEQUENCES
annotations.text: Resource depletion, habitat loss, toxicity, pollution and carbon release occur beyond the apparent boundary of the manufactured object.
